teksten: This is like if Rusty's Retirement had giant scaling issues. The land parcels go from 5,000 gold, to 50,000 gold, to 1,000,000 gold. Yes. You read that right. There might be one more jump in there I'm forgetting, but it's not a 500k, that's for sure. Meanwhile, your crops scale from 10g, to 15g, to 40g, to maybe at this point a max of 56g per harvest, but of course to get that, they take longer to grow even with improved monsters. You can't really have a great deal of land. And suddenly you realise you're making hardly anything at all, even with the tip of the help board / moneytree from a helpful person on the Discussion forum, and you realise this game wants you to play it for months and months and months. It's not a true idler because the storehouse needs to be manually cleared out, and you have to manually submit the quests, and manually click the mushrooms and mouseover the birds, however once you come back to your game after idling for some gold, you spend it all (if you're lucky) on *one* plot of land to grow *one* more 56g crop, before waiting another day or so to do that again. All to get to the 1 mil parcel of land. By the way, that's just the next one, the one after that will cost you more, maybe with crops that pay you, oh, I don't know, 100g. Either the devs are sadists or they don't math good. Just play Rusty's Retirement again. It hurts less.

As much as I like the concept, it just doesn't know what it wants to be. If you leave it alone, as you technically should, monsters sometimes stops working or go somewhere at the end of the map and you gain nothing. But, if you keep playing it, keep trying to engage with it, you'll spend your all gold and crystals in like 2 clicks because prices in game are abysmal. The progress curve is WAY too steep, so it takes around a week / two weeks to casually unlock something. The game tries to be both idle game and full engage game and it fails at both.

PROS + Cute and appealing monster designs. + Beautiful art style. + Interesting farming concept. + Enjoyable early-game progression. + Has considerable potential as a cozy monster-farming game. CONS - Progression becomes very grindy after the early game. - Land acquisition doesn't keep up with crop progression. - Monster optimization relies heavily on RNG. - Fusion and hatching can feel like gambling. - Slow coin economy. - High-grade crops take too long to obtain. VERDICT Your Big, Cute Monster Farm is a game where I really like the idea behind it, but the longer I played, the more its progression systems got in the way of the relaxing experience I wanted. The cute presentation and monster designs give it a lot of potential, but the combination of grind, slow economy, and excessive reliance on RNG makes the game increasingly tiring. I think there's a genuinely good cozy game underneath all of this, but right now, its progression systems need a lot more work to let that potential shine. 2.5/5

Only purchase this game if you’re prepared to spend an entire year completing it. The goals and missions are set absurdly high—virtually unreachable. For instance, a single plot of farmland costs nearly 10 million in the endgame, while each crop earns you only about $100. That means you could spend one to two weeks of grinding just to afford one or two additional plots. You also need to hire monsters to work for you. Even after spending millions—or sometimes billions—you’ll still face strict limits on how many monsters you can use. On top of that, you must buy slots to deploy them. The maximum number of monsters is 36, but expanding to around 20 already costs millions. Expect to grind for days or weeks just to unlock one more plot of farmland or a single monster slot.
Valid but not valid enough — 7/10

Enjoyable concept, bad execution. I enjoyed this game while unlocking the first 10 different crops. The 90% of the game's content after was just a very annoying experience. While the screenshots on the store provide motivation to make an area for every crop, the speed of unlocking crops and the speed of unlocking a decent amount of fields per crop are very different. The game tries to split your focus on targeted crops to unlock more other crops and at the same time produce all crops to be able to cater the board tasks which are certainly a better way to earn currencies after successfully completing the minigame. What I found most annoying was the execution of setting up your helping monsters. Every monster has a rarity and random attributes but to actually optimize you have to rely on gambling with the fusion. I don't see any relaxing value in seeing your progress being dependent on gambling with your currencies...considering this isn't a mobile phone cash grabber, why bother making optimization rely on randomness? I don't see any joy in constantly gambling for monsters with certain attributes and do fusions 24/7 with the hope of keeping as many attributes stick to those attribute slots as possible.

Sure it looks perfectly fine but mechanically it is rather disapointing. Despite continuing to unlock dozens of crops, it never felt like I made any real progress. This is because everything cost way too much and you are rewarded too little. I ended up beating the game without unlocking all the land expansions, so what's the point of making them that expensive? Why even give us expansions if I can't afford them for the majority of the play time??? They needlessly throttle player progression to drag out the length of the game. I stopped feeling any sense of progress after maybe a day. Every new plant that got unlocked felt like it was as useless as they last one. This is because of how bad the plant scaling is. They want you to rely on the order board thing to make money, but because it's so freaking tedious to actually swap your plants out constantly, I just couldn't be bothered. 'You are playing the game wrong.' On god it's an idle farm game, I shouldn't have to min max every single system to make actual progress. It's the same problem with the monster ungrading system. It's so tedius to navigate the menus and actually find the monsters you want to interact with, that trying to create the perfect one by merging traits strategically is way too much of a ♥♥♥♥ around to be bothered with. It doesn't even feel like you have achieved something when you craft the right traits. This is because all the plants are crap anyway and don't reward enough money. Doubling nothing is still nothing. Some of the high tier crops should grow faster, yeild more, give more money I mean come on man. What's even the point of using high tier crops if they are only a fraction better than the one before it? It's completely unsatisfying. The crops just scale uniformly and you never even get a second jewel crop. The way it should work is like this: Faster crops = more water. required Slower crops = more yeild when harvested. Not every end tier crop needs to take a million minutes and require a billion water. When all the crops money per minute rate scale so close together it feels like theres no progress at all. All the decorative blocks are way too underpowered as well, it just feels insulting to go out of my way to build my layout very specifically just so that I can get +8% growth speed at best. It's stupid. Everything in this game is too under-powered and it's really annoying. Not to even mention that the game is rather laggy. I think they intentionally throttle the game in some way so that you can't click the money tree fast enough to actually be effective. And the UI blocking the farm is annoying. I have to open and close the menu multiple times to place stuff around, change crops and reselect tools. It's just another added layer of tedium. I guess if you are so bored that you need to leave a game open for like 10 days just as something else to do every so often... Go for it. Feel free to ignore the feedback and instead make everything 20x more expensive and completely unplayable. I don't know why I bothered.

I love the game but I am not playing for months to just expand to a 6 x 4 area. the gold being switched for fusing is just as ridiculous. So either I am saving for months to expand or I am saving for months to fuse my dream team. If I am waiting months to do anything why the heck am I even playing. Can't lie with about 1000+ hrs in Rusty's Retirement, played all maps umpteen times, at least it was balanced and it doesn't lag. I am off to help Rusty on the farm because it is playable not a waiting game. At this point if you want to stare at monsters farming for months and do nothing. Then it is all you! I do not want to run an idle game that is using half of my memory and not actually be progressing on anything! Thanks!

Having put a hundred hours into this game, I can tell you without a doubt, this game isn't worth it. I don't remember if I bought it on sale or not, but my point still stands at any price point. This game lets you rapidly progress at first and then after maybe 10 crops, the progress grinds to an absolute drip. I have left this game on over night multiple times and still come back to no new crops. At my time of review here, an update has come out recently with new crops. I have very little hope of ever seeing those crops. There is no gameplay because it is an idler. Sure you can click on one tree for one gold each click, but as time goes on, what is even the point if I need a million gold just to buy a crop plot. I can't even make more of that gold producing tree. The game is incredibly unbalanced and progression is a joke. The only form of making things more efficient is your monsters, but you have to gamble to make them better. I saw other reviews mention this fact, but it needs to be mentioned again. I even went to the community tab and you can game the system a bit but it requires a LITERAL ton of currencies and time, plus there is absolutely no guarantee the gambling system doesn't mess up all your hard work. It has pretty graphics and you can let it run in the background, but don't buy this if you want a good product. I highly recommend Rusty's Retirement instead of this game. You can be an active player or just let it run plus it has special collab modes. Play Rusty's instead and save yourself the heartache of this "game."

This was a hard review for me to write as it should have been a big yes, unfortunately this is not the case. I will start with the good: Cute art and nice community. I have had no problems finding groups when I want to party up. The bad: This is falsely advertised as an idler yet there is absolutely no idling in it. This is a clicker and a very basic/boring one at that. There are only a handful of different levels to play, therefore they just keep rotating until you get to 1000. It gets very boring to watch the same 5 levels repeat over and over again. The worst part of this game is the low drop rates for items. Achievement hunters be WARNED. You can either sink 100’s of hours into this just waiting for drops or spend tons of money on marketplace items. I usually love grindy games but this one was just not fun. Way too long for the amount of content offered. If I had known sooner about the lack of gameplay I would have refunded. If you are looking for an idle game well this isn’t one. If you are wanting a clicker game I feel like there are much more fun ones out there.

I don't get why you need the Steam marketplace to implement a player trading function, and why have the odds so woefully low in the first place? Why not allow players to adjust their odds manually or 'Prestige' their characters to improve the odds of their next run? Edit 2: 245 hours in, 204/207 items & 130/160 skins. I'm missing 3 Mythic (highest rarity) items, which are a 1% drop rate that aren't duplication protected, so wish me luck. The 30 skins I'm missing I could just buy off the marketplace like the dev wants me to, but I don't fancy spending a few more £ on a game I've already paid for just to get all the achievements. Edit 3: 286.7 hours to get all achievements. I had to roach out and buy the last 25 skins from the marketplace because I wasn't putting any more time into this 'game' to get them all -- cost me £1.60 in the end.

I really like the concept and the graphics. It’s nice to look at, but unfortunately, that’s where the positives end. Sadly, there are too many downsides that lead me to rate the game negatively. The balancing is really poor, especially for an "idle" game that actually demands a fair amount of active play. You try to adjust your lineup tactically, acquire heroes with better stats, and switch classes, max levels but somehow you inevitably hit a wall at some point. To be honest, it’s quite frustrating. Why does it have to be like that in a single-player idle game? Then there are numerous bugs too. Quest progress sometimes simply doesn't register or there are heroes for whom the auto-equip function just doesn't work at all. The auto-equip feature is also pretty much the worst I’ve ever seen in a game, it often equips much worse items, actually reducing the heroes strength. The itemization is questionable as well. Why are there so many different item classes, yet my archer ends up holding some random gray dagger? Another major annoyance is the font choice, the typeface used is just about the worst possible option they could have picked. Some numbers are impossible to read. It’s a shame, it could have been a great game.

I have waited for almost a month since release, hoping that the devs would reflect on their choices and take a good hard look at the balance between the classes, skills, Mastery types and affixes but after today's update I decided that I will not continue to wait any longer. At this stage, it is more of a beta than an actual full game. Too much is missing, too many things need to be changed/reworked and rebalanced. I do not recommend buying the game as it is right now and suggest waiting for a few major patches first. At least until things have actually been balanced properly and the game feels more like a full game. Many things are out of balance or need a drastic rework. With the latest update, the devs claim they gave compensation skins. Here's the truth: During the demo, only the classes that could be played had some skins. When the full game was released (and they removed the demo) still only those classes that were available during the demo had skins. In other words, they call it "compensation" but in reality, they simply added skins to the game that should have been in already since release. Claiming "compensation" for bad balancing and messing up on translations (many things went from English to Chinese to English to Chinese again over several updates. They are now in English again but I wouldn't be surprised if they ended up being in Chinese again in a future update) is misleading. Their post about a future update including more "compensation skins" is even more misleading. We don't want "compensation skins". We want a fun and balanced game. The demo was closer to an "alpha" version of a game and at the current stage, the game would be closer to a "beta" version. I will explain: A full game has items present that support all possible builds of all classes, even in its base form. This game for example does not have any gems for: * Fire Mastery * Ice Mastery * Lightning Mastery * Poison Mastery * Dark Mastery * Pet Mastery * Lifesteal Mastery * Bleed * Reflect Damage It only has Holy Mastery out of all masteries. Some of the other gems are literally useless. For example: When your heroes have 700+k health, what good are "+1" to "+7" Health Regeneration gems going to do? Monsters and bosses hit for much more so it's "kill or be killed". Each item has 7 gem slots. Even if we were to put a "+7 Health Regeneration" gem in every slot on every item we'd only get 392 Health Regeneration per second. If a boss hits me for 300k every second or so, what good will 392 Health per second do for me? I'd be better off filling everything with Attack Damage or Magic Damage or even Crit Damage. I read that in a future update you want to add more. Awesome, except that the most useless ones (Health Regeneration and Mana Regeneration) will remain useless. There isn't any real choice in what type of gems you put in your items because of the severe lack of balance. The "SSR Slot Machine" item, which lets you reroll affixes in the Forging Table, only has a limited amount of choices and it even rerolls During the demo, you could roll for the "Beast Hunt" affix. When the game was released, it was removed from being rolled for (and added in the Forge through items) and could no longer have it show up on items or get it on your items through the Forge. An update later, it was added to the game again but could not be put as an affix on your items. It was a drop-only type of Affix. Another update later, it was now "Unique". Over the course of several updates since release, several affixes were removed, re-added and made "Unique". I have yet to see an item drop with this Affix however in my hundreds of hours of playing the release version. Someone else has seen it drop (lucky them) though. Meanwhile some other Mastery types have multiple Affixes.... These things not only limit a hero's build (or choices you can make in how you want to build your hero) but the way these are designed by the devs make me wonder if they know what they are doing. "Beast Hunt" being "Unique" (meaning only one of these will work so there's no point in having multiple of this Affix on your weapon) whereas other similar Affixes ("Fire Enchant", "Frost Enchant", "Lightning Enchant", "Weapon Poison", "Dark Corrosion" et cetera) can be stacked (seriously, whoever came up with this design choice needs to think of what they are doing) is ridiculous. To make matters more absurd: There are MULTIPLE affixes for several types of Mastery. Holy Mastery has the most with "Holy Enhancement", "Divine Punishment" (weapon-only apparently, strange choice at this point as it was originally a universal one), "Spirit of Angel" (weapon-only) and "Shaman" (weapon-only). So, dear devs, could you kindly explain to us why some get FOUR different Affixes doing pretty much the same thing while others can't even get one that can be rolled for (or obtained at all)? Holy Mastery: 4 Fire Mastery: 2 Ice Mastery: 2 Lightning Mastery: 3 Dark Mastery: 1 Poison Mastery: 0 Pet Mastery: 0 Lifesteal Mastery: 0 Where's the fairness? Or the balance? (What is your obsession with "Holy"? It's frightening.) With all of the "Unique" affixes being added and Affixes being changed to "Unique" it starts limiting what we can actually put on our items. Some Uniques are very questionable as well. "Steadfast" for example. "Critical hits no longer trigger, but damage dealt is increased by x%" with "x%" being up to 35%. Dear devs, if I have to give up 1000% crit damage (in other words, TEN TIMES more damage) while I'm sitting at 100% crit chance then why would I give that up for a mere 15-35% damage increase? Another thing: Excessive (above 100%) Crit chance is being converted to 2% crit damage for every 1% crit chance. What about dodge chance? Or cooldown reduction? Plenty of hero skills that can give a hero absurd values. For example: My Fire Sorceror has the "Passion" Passive at level 190 which gives: "reduce skill cooldown by 965%". Great, except that cooldown reduction is capped at 70% which makes anything beyond that (and therefore hero Passives that give this beyond the 70%) absolutely useless. It's the same with the dodge Passive and even the "Sudden Rebirth" Passive (25% Chance to instantly revive when summons die, which scales well into the 200+% without adding anything beyond 100%). Basically, any Passive that exceeds a cap (or absolute certainty in the case of "100%") is USELESS above their cap and needs to be reworked to make them useful. Legendary bosses drop a "Corruption Chest". In the past, I would get items of up to level 500-600 from this chest based on the floor level I was on. These days, the Corruption Chest is useless for me. I get level 1800+ items. What would I want a level 450-460 item for? Make them scale with floor levels or Legendary boss difficulty or something…. Legendary boss at "Extreme S" difficulty drops level 3500-3700 gear so why does the Corruption Chest give me 400-500? Devs claim they read the forums. I have brought up the "Beast Hunt" Affix several times. No response whatsoever. During this time, one of the devs literally had not replied to anything for several days (so much for activity) and the other gave some replies but only to some Chinese posts (I guess non-Chinese players don't really matter). At this stage, the game feels, plays and is balanced like an early beta and should not have been released as a full game. There is way too much balancing work to be done. Suggestion for the devs: Stop claiming "compensation" for newly added skins that should have been in since day 1 of release (instead "compensate" us by delivering quality and proper balance), stop adding new Affixes of things that are already in the game (at least until ALL masteries have a fair and equal treatment) and and start fixing and balancing the things that are already in the game first.

The game's save files are local instead of on their servers, so you can modify them however you want (as many other reviews have pointed out). This means that it is impossible to have a full-proof anticheat in place. Now, I don't personally mind this as nothing on the market would be going for more than 3 cents anyways, but what the devs seem to be doing is implementing a bunch of guardrails in the code to prevent people from cheating, which has been detecting many legitimate players as cheaters, or straight out blocking gameplay elements from being accessible and blocking progress. The most obscene example of this is relating to the forge mechanic. You can merge multiple items of the same rarity into an item of the next higher rarity, but after one of the hotfixes a couple days ago, when trying to do so, I am not allowed to do so and get a message "The exchange didn't go through: nothing was forged and your items are still yours. Try again in a moment." For context, the main way to upgrade your gear and progress in this game is via this forge mechanic. There is also an inventory limit, and the only way to clear your inventory is by deleting items for a currency that you have no use for late game and already have way too much of, or by forging them into better items. This just means my inventory has been full for the past couple days and I've been unable to upgrade my character at all, with only 2 legendary items equipped even though I am able to forge Mythic items, which are a tier higher. Another thing that has happened since that hotfix is that the PvP system, (random battles against other player's characters, rewarding EXP and ranked points for the leaderboard) has stopped giving me any exp or RP. I've hit the max level so the EXP doesn't affect me anymore, but not being able to climb the leaderboard is annoying and makes the PvP fights a massive waste of time as they can last upwards of a minute and sometimes happen back to back to back, and can't drop any items. I can only assume that my account was marked suspicious or something due to the half-ass anticheat measures they applied to try and guess if you're cheating or not and so these mechanics have been disabled for me in the background, essentially making the game unplayable. The devs have also been very confident in saying "ALL of the cheaters WILL be banned, we assure you we are just letting them go unbanned to better detect their methods". This is complete BS. There is no way to get 100% of the cheaters if the local save file is what the server trusts. Sure, they can block jumps from level 1 to 60, but what are they going to do if a player gives themself the best item in the game after 100 hours of playtime, it could be legit right? There is no way to tell.

To be frank, this game doesn't value your time or your wallet . And I bet you're saying, "Well, duh, it's an idle game. You just let it idle while you do something else. And it's cheap! What are you talking about." Well, let's get into it. In other idle games the gameplay loop is pretty straight forward. The start of the game is very manual action heavy, requiring your almost constant attention, and slowly, over the course of hours or days, the game automates itself into the background of your life to the point that the game basically plays itself. The enjoyment of it is getting to that point in progression where the numbers get big and the amount of effort is minimal. ... Deskrawler doesn't really get there? The issue with the game comes down to its premise- it's an ARPG . ARPGs live or die by loot drops. If loot drops are garbage, you get release day Diablo 3. If loot drops are rare, but build defining, you get Diablo 2. If loot drops are plentiful and awesome, you get the original Borderlands. You see where I'm going here- the more unique, the more diverse, the more plentiful the loot, the more enjoyable the game becomes. Right now this game is very very first day of release Diablo 3. Loot is rare, terrible, and generally just long stat sticks with nothing of value to them besides bigger number = better. It's frustrating. Your entire progression becomes loot focused to the point that you could be several levels above the enemies you're fighting just because your gear isn't good enough to fight things at your level. And, you will end up at a higher level than enemies. You eventually unlock the ability to get hours worth of progress when the game is closed, but this only applies to getting gold and experience. Gold doesn't actually do anything in this game. You can't buy loot with it; instead, you use it, primarily, to upgrade the gear you have (and I'm talking like 0.1 more attack speed or 1% more damage per upgrade) or buy meta passives (like 10% more experience, item find, etc, etc). Eventually you will get to the point that you're just idling to find loot to progress- and loot is very very rare. But, remember when I said this game was like Diablo 3 on release day? The comparison is more apt than you think. Just like Diablo 3 at release, this game also has a real money auction house. You can buy stuff with actual money. Because drop rates are so low, even in the offline mode where you can't use the auction house, it creates this very Diablo 3 predatory real money auction house dynamic. I didn't know about this until I started writing this review. I had been playing offline where the drop rate is so bad that I thought that I must have been doing something wrong. Nope. I wasn't. The game is designed this way. Even with my meta item find passives maxed out, finding decent gear takes hours. And, again, this is the way the game is designed. It's meant to push you towards online mode, which still has terrible drop rates, in the chance that you use the real money auction house. Because, guess what, the developers get a 10% cut of all those real money market transactions. It directly benefits the developer to have low drop rates to funnel people into, basically, microtransactions- which aren't actually that micro when you see that items are selling for $20+. The thing that really chaps me about this? When I played the demo during Next Fest, the item drops were way higher. This tells me that the developers have intentionally bombed item drop rates in all modes purely to get that sweet revenue cut from the market place. It behooves the developer's pockets to have rarer item drops. Sadly, this ruins the player experience to the point that I don't think anyone should purchase this game... Because this isn't a game- it's glorified crypto. You idle for the off chance of finding an item you can sell on the market. The only person this benefits is the developer who both designed the system and gets a cut of those transactions. So, yeah, the game doesn't respect your time or your money or you . Don't buy this game. Don't support this nonsense.

Idle games transitioning from the early game push to the mid game stalling and into the end game grind is a hard path to tread properly. Some games abruptly hit a torturous grind so quickly that you just throw your hands up and uninstall because, well, this is the number go up game. Number not going up. I am effectively locked out of what passes for endgame content because nothing drops. "Oh, you're being hyperbolic," you say. No. I hit the endgame grind, in which gear of three more rarities begin dropping, and haven't seen a single piece in a week of straight farming. I haven't even gotten the legendary reins from the map I've been farming. Things just don't drop. At all. I've had this game running for 300 hours, how have I not gotten a drop at all. It doesn't actually take all that long to hit endgame. Online play chases best times and leaderboards for specific maps. There is no point in doing so because the top people all shilled out $100 on the Steam marketplace to get a full set of the best items anyone's gotten to drop while you're lucky if you've seen a piece, and to be honest, it kinda feels like you'll have a better experience with this game if you sell whatever you manage to get to drop so you can at least make your money back on this game. Which, fun fact, gives the developer money. Huh, a game I respected for not having microtransactions has microtransactions. Can you feel the negative Sims interaction icon over my head through my typing? I'm no stranger to grindy games. I love me a bit of Dragon Quest 9, where it takes 45 hours to hit the end of the game and a thousand to properly finish it in its entirety. The post mid-game loop is rushing grotto map chests to farm that rare 2% treasure chest good item drop chance just so you can fail a 5% chance success rate on the item you're making and get to do it all over again. This is after you've spent hundreds of hours farming your levels enough that you can even get a decent map with decent treasure chests. You can get so granular in that game's farming that you can farm stat point increasing consumables, one at a time, to increase all your party to 999 stats, 1-3 points at a time. There was at least a line of progression in both of these. You felt like your time wasn't being disrespected outright, what with all the other things you got out of the chests and the slow drip of the stat point consumables. And this game has... farming one mission, over and over again, so you can farm the rifts, and get nothing from either of them. Neat. I'm remembering why I never seriously considered Diablo. Check back in a year or two. Either the devs will give this more time or they won't.

I wrote a whole thing about how it took three weeks for me to realize exactly what was wrong with this game, but it got long and boring so here's the moderately shorter version: It feels cheap and poorly put together. The weapon model rendered on your character frequently looks nothing like the inventory icon, all of the inventory/store/etc. screens are clunky and awkward and seem to have no discernible logic to how they behave, and some of the UI/UX design decisions are so mindbogglingly terrible they are actually kind of funny (eg, hovering over your health potion to prepare to drink one causes a tooltip popup that BLOCKS YOUR HEALTH ORB). The itemization is so boring and uninspired it's actually kind of impressive. The only "exciting" drops are Divine gear and set runes; everything has almost entirely randomized stats and will be useless 95%+ of the time. So even if you know you want that Serrated Greatsword of Agony, seeing one drop is completely unremarkable because the odds of it actually being worth using are vanishingly small. The game almost seems like it's going for the launch D3 route, where the good stuff is so rare people will be driven to the RMAH to buy it and the devs can take a cut - which is a ridiculous system to have in an idle game. The final straw for me was when I found an item that was objectively better than what I had in every metric, and when I equipped it my dps fell by over 40%. Either the damage calculations are bugged, or they are so arcane and convoluted that that was intended behavior; in either case, the primary purpose of an idle game is to make interesting decisions and then let them play out in real time (with some random events sprinkled in as rewards); if the decisions I make have turned out to be mostly arbitrary, I don't see any reason to keep playing.

The concept of endless skill tree sounds pretty good. Unfortunately, this game just isn't very interesting. After 18h, I had 100% achievements. I had unlocked ALL unlocks after abour 10h. Very short for a pure idle game. As an Idlegame, there is no gameplay, the game runs (except for one upgrade) on its own. While it's doing it's thing, it's not particularily interesting to look at, mostly you are waiting on it to farm skillpoints or diamonds. The gameplay must be the choices on the skill tree, but apart from choosing which basic mechanics you want to be even able to get, there is very little variance in the skill tree. You cannot navigate to multi-shot-side or something like that, each little blob of skills is 100% random. This defeats long term planning. The update that adds some rarer nodes helps a bit, but it pretty much just gives a bit more stats. The skills you can get on the skill tree basically affect one of the mechanics. Firespeed, base damage, knockback, and then each mechanic has ONE variance of upgrade you get for it. Multishot gets +20% chance of multishotting, turrets have +1 turret, and so on. Each of the added mechanics aren't very deep. Balancing wise, some feel mandatory, and some feel absolutely useless. Bounce regularily misses the bounced target and is 100% useless against single bosses. Shield ALWAYS completely resets all enemies encrouching to the furthest point. This is mandatory. I found most success with ignoring most mechanics, just picking things that DIRECTLY multiply my damage (multishot, critchance, crit dmg). Thats fairly boring balance. I 100%ed the game without killing the boss for wave 220, which has a few billion HP. Far from infinite. The game doesn't offer some sort of statisticsview that displays finer details about what deals how much damage. Mechanics are described very simply and as a player you are left alone in how they interact with each other (mostly they don't). Multishots cannot crit for example (without an upgrade). The prestigue system just gives you damage multiplier, experience multiplier or diamond gain multiplier. It can unlock some things, but there is no choice what to unlock and there are way too few things to unlock. It feels more like getting things you should have from the beginning. It's very boring as a system. The game, especially after dying or prestiguing isn't running fast enough. Going through 100 trivial waves takes a long time. My wishlist to make this game better: - Prestigue needs to be interesting somehow. - Let me focus on a build. The quest system works AGAINST that. Make scaling into "just rockets" work and fun. - Improve the tutorials/descriptions. I have 100%ed the game and I couldn't tell you how much damage most mechanics will do. - Make the skill tree more varied, more interesting and more plannable. As a player, I want to look at the skill tree and plan what to focus.

Cool little game inspired by Diablo. 15 hours in it's a basic/simple idle taskbar game. The idea is great but I'm hoping to see more stuff added since I've already almost completed the game. In these 15 hours I've reached the last level on Nightmare but haven't got enough gold for an Ascension. It seems it gives you some bonus stats and you just repeat the levels. For $3 you get what you pay for, definitely worth the money if they add the usual; Crafting affix/suffix, unique gear/stats, skills and so on. At the moment you just swap for better gear and buy talents (basic ones) for gold and let it run until you can afford Ascension to repeat it all. Should be a demo or something, definitely unfinished.

Way too shallow to be any fun. Talent tree exists but are just generic, tiny stat upgrades like 5% gold find, 8% dmg, 5% armor. 1% crit. 3 active skills (HUGE amount!) but only 1 can be equipped, and each has 2x2=4 (HUGE amount again!) branching choices. No gear inventory, you get a queue of ~5 dropped pieces of gear waiting in line, and you decide whether each piece is worn or sold (and when new piece is worn, the replaced piece just gets sold too). And that's it! There is no build depth - or rather, not even 'builds' to begin with; there's no character progression; there's no meaningful itemization. Even with a low price tag this is hardly worth your time, at all.

The game is broken. I modded the annoyances, like the hidden tech tree (unhid it), burying auto-sell in the tree (I enable it by default), and increasing the review queue. It still was pretty weak. So I added a time (x) toggle, 1, 2 and 4x speeds. It's then I found out this game is basically broken. I let it run on high speed through to Agony 10. It showed that the progression is total garbage. Even on high difficulty you repeat the lower levels the loot doesn't scale up so you are getting the same drops as if you were level 10.. Also, the tech tree is fully unlocked after a pretty fast period of time and there is nothing to do with the money after this. So you end the game on Agony X with 30,000,000 gold and nothing to buy. The grind is unbelievable, but the grind for what? There is no meta progression. Speeding it up to 4X it finished in 20 hours. I assume leaving it at normal speed would be 4x that and for what? Nothing. It ends and nothing happens. I don't consider it terrible, but it certainly isn't a good game. If it was any more than a dollar or two I'd of felt ripped off.
